name: Jigdalja
title: Man of God
summary: Jigdalja is a little-known biblical figure mentioned only once in Scripture, in Jeremiah 35:4. He is referred to as 'Man of God' and was the father of Hanan, whose sons had a chamber in the temple in Jerusalem. His title 'Man of God' suggests he may have been a prophet or a man with spiritual authority.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in connection with the Rechabites' test
keyEvents.description: Jigdalja is mentioned as the father of Hanan, whose sons' chamber in the temple was used by the prophet Jeremiah when he tested the Rechabites with wine.

keyEvents.title: The Chamber of His Grandsons in the Temple
keyEvents.description: The sons of Hanan, son of Jigdalja, had their own chamber in the house of the Lord, indicating that the family held a recognized position among the temple servants.

keyEvents.title: Referred to as 'Man of God'
keyEvents.description: Jigdalja is given the honored title 'Man of God', a designation usually used in the Old Testament for prophets and persons with special spiritual authority, such as Moses and Elijah.

keyEvents.title: Context: The Faithfulness of the Rechabites
keyEvents.description: The event where Jigdaljah is mentioned concerns the Rechabites' faithfulness to the command of their ancestor Jonadab. Jeremiah used their obedience as an example to rebuke Judah for their disobedience to God.
